name: Abdul Samad Zeeshan
intro: I finished my Computing Science degree at the University of Alberta in June 2026. I build backend services, data pipelines and systems with a language model somewhere inside. Each project below takes one real problem and reports its numbers as they came out, including the bad ones.

edges.evidence: The agent, the MCP server and the risk engine are Python, and the results tables are rebuilt from files in eval.
A LangGraph agent does the legwork on each change request but never holds the power to approve anything alone.
0 of 84 prompt-injection attacks got through the hardened build over MCP on HTTP, against 35 of 84 with the boundary layers off.
Tools arrive only when a step needs them, and the write role only arrives after the risk is assessed.
Each credential is short-lived and bound to one customer and one request. 7 forgery techniques got 0 calls served.
The hardened build also held at 0 of 84 attacks against live Keycloak and Postgres.
Policy is a versioned file, checked with z3 against the previous version on every update.
A test fails if any results table in the README drifts from the files in eval.
The simulator, the recording proxy and the report are Python, tested with pytest.
Tests an AI agent on simulated customers, with its tools recorded or faked so nothing real is touched.
Paired intervals decide each hypothesis. Planted tool calls reaching Warden's server fell from 1.301 to 0.607 per scenario over 336 scenarios.
Three transcript judges were calibrated on anchors and scored against the tool state on 240 sampled calls.
A run recorded with a local model replays in CI with no model at all.
A Java service on the JDK's HTTP server, with virtual threads and hand-written JSON.
Postgres constraints back the ledger rules: a unique idempotency key, a balance check and non-zero postings.
A payment retried after a lost reply lands exactly once. 1,580 retries across the fault runs, 0 applied twice.
Account rows are locked in one fixed order, so two crossing transfers cannot deadlock.
A TLA+ model follows the transfer code statement by statement and passes over 394,177 distinct states.
11,054 transfers through 7 fault runs on Kubernetes, with 0 violations of any kind.
A kind cluster from plain Kustomize manifests, with four deployment gates and a fault gate.
Graph rules reach 0.8179 fraud precision on a fresh seed, against 0.3655 for the v1 rules.
A verifier recomputed 16 features for all 9,290 postings and found 0 mismatches with the Java scorer.
Hand-written Prometheus metrics, and latency measured open loop from the scheduled send time.
A small, fixed HTTP API over the ledger with no framework.
CI repeats the fault runs on every push as the fifth gate.
The dialogue layer, the booking API and the eval are Python, with a test suite that needs no models.
faster-whisper and Piper on one CPU with no network. 17 of 40 scripted calls booked end to end over audio.
232 of 232 calls that hit a booking API fault were handled safely, with 0 false facts spoken.
The same scripted calls are replayed with clean audio, stressed audio, corrupted transcripts and a failing backend.
The booking API is made slow, empty, contradictory or down mid-call, and Parley queues a callback instead of guessing.
CI fails if the README tables drift from the results file.
The detector, the verifier and the scoring are Python over a local lake of the full log.
Batch and Spark streaming share one feature engine over the full log of 1,051,430,459 events.
The v1 platform keeps a dbt and DuckDB warehouse over the login lake.
Logins are scored as each one arrives, and logins in the same second never see each other.
The v1 platform keeps a Neo4j graph of which user logged into which computer.
5,079,642 point-in-time features recomputed with the future cut off, 0 mismatches.
29 of 181 attack account-days caught at 100 alerts a day, against 21 for v1's rules.
Every detector learns only from day 0 and is scored against the lab's answer key, bad results included.
An AI analyst asks graph questions through a closed tool registry, and invented calls are refused.
The analyst's calibration error was 0.04 with graph tools and 0.05 without, on the 49 alerts it finished.
CI runs the same code on a committed 99,434-event slice and fails if the tables drift.
The training and evaluation pipeline is Python.
A 600M-parameter model fine-tuned with LoRA reaches 87.3% priority accuracy on 1,200 held-out tickets, against 38.3% for the base model.
A hosted teacher labels the tickets and the small model learns from those labels.
Returns category, priority and account id as JSON, offline, with no API call.
89.7% category accuracy on the same 1,200 tickets, against 64.2% for the base model.
The pipeline, its tests and its eval are TypeScript.
S3, EventBridge, SQS, Lambda and DynamoDB. Deployed to a test account, checked end to end, then torn down.
20 of 20 public photo answers were valid JSON with the grammar, against 17 of 20 without it.
Claude Haiku 4.5 on Bedrock scored 0.999 field accuracy on 42 hand checked receipts, from saved responses.
At a 1% field error budget, 11 of 149 test receipts pass with no person, and 0 of their 32 fields are wrong.
Ids hash the bucket, key and ETag with a conditional write, so a redelivery never makes a second record.
CloudWatch alarms publish to an SNS topic that grants the right in writing, after TLS enforcement silently removed the default grant.
